# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆 ☝ ✌ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌]

I see the bomb: display shows 3, light is purple, and five wires in order: red, white, orange, yellow, green. I hear nothing, so I have no speech context. I received gestures from Blind and Mute (I can see them since I'm Deaf... wait, actually I'm Deaf — I can see gestures). Let me re-read.

Actually as Deaf I *can* see gestures. The context says Blind gestured to Deaf and Mute gestured to Deaf. So I received those gestures. But the symbols are just symbols to me — I don't know what they mean yet. I need to coordinate. I can speak to Mute and Blind, and gesture to Mute only.

My job: describe the bomb to the others. Mute has the manual and can read it, but cannot speak — so Mute must gesture to me (I can see) and I relay to Blind by speaking. Blind can feel the bomb and act, but cannot see. So I need to tell Blind what I see, and Mute needs to tell me what the manual says.

Let me send my observations. Blind can hear speech, so I speak to Blind. Mute can hear speech too (Mute can't speak but can hear). So I'll speak to both — describe the bomb.

I should describe everything clearly: display 3, purple light, wires red-white-orange-yellow-green.

I can't yet interpret the gestures from Blind/Mute. But I should share my view.

Let me speak to both (unnamed reaches Mute and Blind).I can see the bomb, so my job is to get its description to Blind (who acts) and to coordinate with Mute (who reads the manual). I received gestures but don't yet know their meaning. Let me broadcast my full view of the bomb first.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb view: DISPLAY shows 3. LIGHT is purple. Five wires left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Tell me what the manual says and I will relay. What can you feel?")
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: DISPLAY shows 3. LIGHT is purple. Five wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Please gesture the manual's rules to me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👊 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

I received new gestures: Blind sent [👌 👊 ✋] and Mute sent [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]. I still don't know the alphabet mapping — gestures are only meaningful once someone establishes meaning. But I can relay what I see and try to get the manual's rules.

Mute sent five ☝ symbols — five of something. Could be "wire 5" or "five wires" or a count. Blind sent three symbols.

I need the manual's rules. Mute can hear my speech and can gesture back. Let me ask Mute directly to spell out the rule for the current display/light/wires.

I should also relay to Blind. But Blind can't see gestures, only hear speech. So I must speak to Blind.

Let me ask Mute to give me the rule clearly, and tell Blind what I currently know.

I can't interpret gestures yet. Let me establish a convention: ask Mute to gesture the wire number to cut, or the rule. Actually Mute reads the manual — the manual likely has rules conditioned on display number, light color, wire colors. Mute needs to tell me which rule applies, and I relay to Blind.

Let me speak to Mute asking for the rule, and speak to Blind with current status.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 3, purple light, wires red white orange yellow green. Gesture me the manual rule that applies: which wire to cut, and any condition. Spell it symbol by symbol and I will relay to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Still waiting on manual rules from Mute. Current bomb: display 3, purple light, wires red white orange yellow green. Do not cut yet. What do you feel on the bomb — any markings, serial, ports?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I received: Blind [👎 ✋ 👌], Mute [✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝] and [🖐].

I still have no established meaning for gestures. But I notice Mute now sent ✊ followed by five ☝. Earlier Mute sent five ☝ alone. Now ✊ + five ☝. And a separate 🖐.

I cannot interpret these without a convention. I need to establish meaning. But gestures are one-way to me — I can't gesture back meaningfully since only Mute sees my gestures and Mute can't speak. Actually I CAN gesture to Mute (Mute sees gestures). So I can gesture back to Mute to confirm.

But wait — the real issue: I need the manual's rule. Mute reads the manual and gestures to me. I relay to Blind by speech. Blind acts.

Let me try to establish a simple code with Mute: ask Mute to gesture wire number. But I can't hear Mute and Mute can't speak. We can only use gestures. I can gesture a proposed convention and Mute can respond.

Alternatively, maybe the gestures ARE the manual content and I should interpret them as-is if there's a natural mapping. But "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something."

Let me propose a convention to Mute: I'll gesture ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, etc. Actually the alphabet has numbers? The symbols list doesn't include digit gestures explicitly but ☝ could be 1.

Let me be practical. I'll gesture to Mute a request: "spell the wire number using ☝ repeated" — i.e., confirm that N taps of ☝ means wire N. Mute sent five ☝ — maybe meaning wire 5? And ✊ could mean "cut".

Actually: Mute [✊ ☝☝☝☝☝] could be "cut wire 5" if ✊ = cut and ☝x5 = 5. And [🖐] = 5 too (five fingers). So Mute may be saying wire 5.

But I shouldn't guess. Let me confirm with Mute via gesture, and meanwhile relay to Blind.

Hmm, but I can only gesture to Mute (Mute sees). Blind doesn't see gestures. So to confirm with Mute I gesture.

Let me gesture to Mute: ask "does ✊ mean cut?" I can't easily ask yes/no without convention. Let me just propose: I'll gesture the wire number I think, and Mute confirms.

Actually simpler: I'll speak to Mute (Mute hears) asking Mute to confirm by gesturing 👍 for yes / 👎 for no. That establishes meaning.

Let me do that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirm: gesture 👍 if ✊ means CUT and five ☝ means wire 5. Gesture 👎 if not. Also: does the manual rule for display 3 purple light give a specific wire?")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute may be indicating wire 5 (green). Hold. Confirm before cutting. Any markings on the bomb?")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👊 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute gestured 👍 — yes. So my proposed meaning is confirmed: ✊ = CUT, and five ☝ = wire 5. Mute also repeated [✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝] = "cut wire 5". Wire 5 is green.

Blind gestured [✋ 👊 ☝] — unknown, but Blind can't see gestures... wait, Blind gestured to Deaf. Blind can feel the bomb and can gesture. So Blind is gesturing findings. I can't interpret yet.

But I have a clear instruction from Mute (the manual reader): cut wire 5. I must relay to Blind by speech, since Blind can't see gestures.

Let me confirm the rule once more and relay. Actually Mute confirmed. Let me relay to Blind: cut wire 5 (green).

But wait — I should double check: is ✊ = cut, or did 👍 just confirm my whole question? I asked "gesture 👍 if ✊ means CUT and five ☝ means wire 5." Mute gave 👍. So yes, cut wire 5.

Let me relay to Blind clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Manual says: CUT WIRE 5 — the GREEN wire. That is confirmed by Mute. Please cut wire 5 now.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤜 ✊]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb changed. New state: DISPLAY 7, LIGHT white, wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 CUT (gone).

Blind gestured [👌 🤜 ✊]. I can't interpret yet.

Now I need the manual's rule for display 7, white light, four remaining wires. Let me ask Mute. My established convention: ✊ = cut, ☝ repeated = wire number. Let me also confirm the light color matters — but Mute can't see the bomb, so I must tell Mute the new state.

Let me speak to Mute with the new state and ask for the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb state: DISPLAY 7, LIGHT white, wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red. Wire 5 already cut. Gesture the wire to cut next using ✊ = cut and ☝ repeated = wire number.")
speak(to="blind", text="New state: display 7, white light, wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red. Waiting on manual rule from Mute. Hold.")
```
